title: Aggrega Catalog (ArtifactLibrary)
description: A reusable collection of named artifact bundles that Recipes and FeatureRecipes consume at render time via `artifacts.<name>: { $import: ... }`. Each bundle is a set of output files imported as one unit. Tier 3 — opt-in for catalogs that need cross-Recipe artifact reuse. Single authoring mode: Go templates only.

name.description: PascalCase identifier for the library. It is the <Library> name in the bare-name identity reference <Library>#/artifacts/<name>; the version is supplied by the per-Release lockfile and no registry host enters the reference or any derived identifier.

version.description: Strict Semantic Versioning of the library (e.g., 1.0.0). A consumer may assert this as an optional `:<version>` minimum-version floor in a bare-name reference (<Library>:<version>#/artifacts/<name>); the per-Release lockfile owns the resolved version.

description.description: A concise summary of what the library covers.

labels.description: Author-declared labels. The compiler is content-neutral and does not interpret label values: they are opaque metadata, carried for whatever reads the library to match on.

annotations.description: Author-declared annotations. Same opaque-metadata posture as labels.

propertyNames.description: PascalCase identifier. Entry keys appear in canonical reference URLs (`#/artifacts/<name>`); the envelope-level constraint prevents non-PascalCase keys from propagating through the catalog ecosystem. The <name> addresses the whole bundle, never an individual file within it.

additionalProperties.description: One file in the bundle. The value is a Go template fragment authored as a YAML string whose output is the artifact body emitted to that file. The compiler stores the fragment verbatim at ArtifactLibrary load; parsing happens at consumption time when the bundle is imported via `artifacts.<name>: { $import: ... }`.

A named bundle: a map of filename to Go-template file body. Importing the bundle at a single `artifacts.<name>` site expands into one output per file, each nested under the key the bundle was imported at as `<key>/<filename>`. Each filename names the bundle's own file within that key and is otherwise free-form, so it may carry a nested layout such as `rbac/role.yaml`; it must be an ordinary relative file name written plainly, and a build refuses one that names no file of its own beneath the key — `.`, `./`, a name that collapses back onto the key such as `x/..`, a trailing or doubled `/`, a `.` or `..` part, an absolute name or one that climbs out. At least one file is required.

artifacts.description: Named map of reusable artifact bundles. Each bundle groups the output files that belong together (for example a CRD, its RBAC, and a ConfigMap). Each file body is opaque to the envelope validation — content semantics are handled by the Go template parser at consumption time.

spec.description: The ArtifactLibrary's content. spec.artifacts is required and must declare at least one bundle. spec carries additionalProperties: false — no parallel authoring modes are accepted at the envelope level. The single-authoring-mode posture keeps rendering uniform (Go template throughout) and avoids forcing authors to switch evaluation models mid-render when consuming imported bundles.
